title: The double submit
context: A developer asked an AI assistant to handle a 'Place Order' button click that charges a customer's card and creates an order record. The suggested code works fine for a single click, but customers who double-click the button, or click again while the page is slow to respond, sometimes get charged twice.
question: Why can a customer end up charged twice from a single order attempt?
options: Nothing disables the button or guards against re-entry while the first click's async work is still in flight, so a second click before it resolves starts a second, fully independent chargeCard call.
chargeCard automatically retries once if the network is slow, doubling the charge.
React batches the two await calls into a single request, doubling cart.total.
onClick handlers in React always fire twice in production builds.

explanation.theBug: The button stays enabled and clickable for the entire duration of the async handleClick call. If a customer double-clicks, or clicks again because the page feels unresponsive while chargeCard and createOrder are still pending, a second, completely independent handleClick invocation starts — running chargeCard(cart.total) a second time before the first one has even finished. Nothing in this code tracks whether a submission is already in progress.
explanation.whyAIGeneratesThis: The handler correctly implements the happy path — click once, charge once — and that's exactly what gets tested manually. Guarding against rapid double-clicks or re-entrant submissions is a UX and reliability concern that has to be explicitly requested; it isn't implied by 'handle the button click,' so the model has no strong signal to include it unprompted.

theFix.commentary: Track an in-flight flag and disable the button while it's true — standard practice for any button that triggers a payment or a write with real-world side effects.

explanation.reviewHeuristic: Any button that triggers a non-idempotent action — a charge, a write, an email — needs a submitting guard; assume users will double-click or click while the page looks frozen.
